scope: read existing JSON only; no inference, audio render, playback candidate, score or database mutation
grid: Each consecutive existing quarter-note beat interval is divided into 4 equal parts (primary 16th); 8 parts (32nd) reference only. No fixed BPM, no swing/triplet assumption tested. Use bracketing beats, no extrapolation.
mapping: Nearest existing subdivision point by absolute distance; ties within 1e-12 seconds go earlier. Preserve all input note identities, original onsets, ends and pitches. Mapped onsets are diagnostic fields only.
collision: Two or more distinct sequential notes mapped to the same grid point. Report groups, all involved notes, excess occupants sum(k-1), adjacent equal-pitch pairs, and all original durations/pitches. Excess is not actual deletion.
gate: Any G collision blocks a no-deletion/no-merge listening proposal under this rule. Zero collisions only passes onset feasibility, not duration/rest/repetition or accuracy. No extremely-few threshold.
SOME: Read raw offset+durations+rest flags; accumulate rests; preserve continuous pitch, report rounded MIDI for comparison only; compare identities/times to frozen MIDI-derived notes.
edges: Nearest point can lie just outside clip; flag separately, do not clamp. Non-bracketed onset fails coverage. Small source-origin rounding difference remains explicit.
human_scope: third-1 click confirmation; saved-G uses accepted accompaniment grid, not independent proof of sixteenth-note vocal rhythm
extension: User allows a further two days if a concrete idea merits it; no automatic experiment after this count, 60-minute cap retained.
